nativeaot-reflection-trimming.title: Use reflection safely with NativeAOT and trimming
nativeaot-reflection-trimming.short: Tell static analysis which members dynamic access requires
nativeaot-reflection-trimming.summary: NativeAOT and trimming cannot always infer members reached only through runtime reflection.
nativeaot-reflection-trimming.why: DynamicallyAccessedMembers and related annotations help prevent members from disappearing only after publishing a trimmed application.
nativeaot-reflection-trimming.tips: Prefer source generation or static type references where practical, and annotate only the member categories the code truly requires.

libraryimport-source-generated-pinvoke.title: Generate P/Invoke stubs with LibraryImport
libraryimport-source-generated-pinvoke.short: Generate interop marshalling code at build time
libraryimport-source-generated-pinvoke.summary: LibraryImportAttribute source-generates native-call stubs and reduces dependence on runtime stub generation.
libraryimport-source-generated-pinvoke.why: It fits AOT scenarios better and makes supported marshalling paths more explicit.
libraryimport-source-generated-pinvoke.tips: Declare the method partial and make every string, struct, and calling convention choice match the native ABI.

httpclient-responseheadersread-streaming.title: Stream HTTP response bodies with HttpClient
httpclient-responseheadersread-streaming.short: Start reading the body as soon as response headers arrive
httpclient-responseheadersread-streaming.summary: ResponseHeadersRead lets code process a response stream without buffering the complete body first.
httpclient-responseheadersread-streaming.why: Large downloads and incremental parsers can reduce peak memory and begin useful work sooner.
httpclient-responseheadersread-streaming.tips: Dispose both the response and body stream and propagate cancellation through every read operation.

activitysource-distributed-tracing.title: Instrument distributed traces with ActivitySource
activitysource-distributed-tracing.short: Represent operation spans as Activity instances with tags
activitysource-distributed-tracing.summary: ActivitySource starts Activity spans whose parent relationships and tags can flow into diagnostics and telemetry systems.
activitysource-distributed-tracing.why: Operations that cross service boundaries can be correlated on one trace to find latency and failure points.
activitysource-distributed-tracing.tips: Keep hot paths cheap when no listener is present and never place secrets in activity tags.

aspnetcore-request-cancellation.title: Propagate request cancellation in ASP.NET Core
aspnetcore-request-cancellation.short: Pass the disconnected request token into downstream work
aspnetcore-request-cancellation.summary: ASP.NET Core exposes request aborts as CancellationToken values that can flow into database, network, and other asynchronous operations.
aspnetcore-request-cancellation.why: Expensive work can stop after the client leaves instead of consuming server resources for an abandoned response.
aspnetcore-request-cancellation.tips: Pass the same token through downstream APIs and avoid reporting ordinary request cancellation as a flood of application failures.

cancellationtoken-register-resource-clea.title: Use CancellationToken.Register to release blocking resources
cancellationtoken-register-resource-clea.short: Run a cancellation callback that closes a resource which cannot accept a token
cancellationtoken-register-resource-clea.summary: CancellationToken.Register can bridge cancellation into waits or external resources whose APIs do not directly accept a CancellationToken.
cancellationtoken-register-resource-clea.why: Legacy APIs and blocking resource waits can be interrupted when cancellation is requested instead of being abandoned indefinitely.
cancellationtoken-register-resource-clea.tips: Dispose the CancellationTokenRegistration to bound its lifetime and make the callback safe against races with normal completion.

loh-allocation-pressure.title: Understand Large Object Heap allocation pressure
loh-allocation-pressure.short: Manage the lifetime and reuse of large buffers to reduce GC pressure
loh-allocation-pressure.summary: Large objects are placed on the Large Object Heap, where frequent allocation and retirement can affect pauses and memory usage.
loh-allocation-pressure.why: Hot paths that repeatedly create large buffers have different costs from ordinary small temporary allocations.
loh-allocation-pressure.tips: Measure first, then consider pooling or chunked processing when those approaches match the required lifetime and capacity.

lock-contention-hot-path.title: Keep expensive work out of contended lock regions
lock-contention-hot-path.short: Protect shared state for the shortest correct critical section
lock-contention-hot-path.summary: Doing I/O or heavy computation while holding a lock forces unrelated threads to wait for work that does not itself require exclusivity.
lock-contention-hot-path.why: The program can remain correct while losing parallelism and developing long wait chains under load.
lock-contention-hot-path.tips: Move independent work outside the critical section without splitting operations whose shared-state invariants must remain atomic.

loggermessage-source-generated-logging.title: Source-generate hot-path logging with LoggerMessage
loggermessage-source-generated-logging.short: Generate typed logging code and avoid repeated formatting overhead
loggermessage-source-generated-logging.summary: LoggerMessageAttribute generates strongly typed logging methods for frequently executed logging sites.
loggermessage-source-generated-logging.why: Hot paths can avoid avoidable formatting and argument-allocation costs while keeping structured log fields.
loggermessage-source-generated-logging.tips: Do not mechanically convert every log call; prioritize paths where measurement shows logging overhead matters.

false-sharing-concurrent-counters.title: Avoid false sharing in concurrent counters
false-sharing-concurrent-counters.short: Independent variables can still contend when they share a cache line
false-sharing-concurrent-counters.summary: Threads updating adjacent independent values may repeatedly transfer ownership of the same cache line between CPU cores.
false-sharing-concurrent-counters.why: Values that are logically unshared can still scale poorly because of their physical memory layout.
false-sharing-concurrent-counters.tips: Confirm the effect with profiling or benchmarks before introducing padding or more complex aggregation layouts.
